name: Thanh Toan Bridge
kicker: Tiled bridge in the vegetable plots
summary: Cycle out to the tiled bridge in Thủy Thanh, about 8 km southeast of the centre. The national tourism page describes a roof about 17 metres long and about 4 metres wide, in seven compartments, with a shrine to Trần Thị Đào. The fee, the hours, and the ride in minutes are check on arrival.
getThere: About 8 km southeast, through the plots. Minutes are check on arrival.
heroCaption: The tiled roof of Thanh Toan Bridge over the lilies

notice.title: No published fee, and no published hour
notice.body: Vietnam Tourism describes the bridge and the cycle. It does not print a ticket or a closing time. A missing line is not free entry. Confirm the gate when you arrive.

body: The national tourism page places Thanh Toan about 8 kilometres southeast of the centre, in Thủy Thanh commune, Hương Thủy. Vietnam Tourism’s Hue page sends a bicycle past vegetable plots and small footbridges. The kilometres are not a minute count.

The same national page describes a bridge about 17 metres long and about 4 metres wide, divided into seven compartments. The middle compartment is a shrine to Trần Thị Đào, who funded the bridge in the 18th century so the village could cross. A later national article gives a slightly different length. The visit is the roof and the shrine, not a rebuilt measurement.
No fee and no hour are on those pages. Check on arrival. How long the cycle from the south bank takes is check on arrival too.

figures.caption: The decorated portal of the tiled bridge
figures.alt: A carved portal under the tiled roof of Thanh Toan Bridge

gettingThere: From the south bank, cycle southeast about 8 km to Thủy Thanh, Hương Thủy. Vietnam Tourism describes the way as vegetable plots and footbridges. The minutes are check on arrival.

legs.heading: From the south bank
legs.body: Bicycle, about 8 km southeast. No published minute count. Check on arrival.

closed: No closing day is published. Confirm on arrival.
admissionNote: Check on arrival. No fee is printed on the national tourism page.
